result.summary: This residential street features row houses and embedded trolley tracks but lacks basic pedestrian safety infrastructure such as marked crosswalks or curb ramps. The presence of narrow sidewalks provides some separation, but the overall design prioritizes vehicle storage and movement over pedestrian connectivity.

hazards.name: Embedded Trolley Tracks
hazards.description: Steel tracks in the roadway create a tripping hazard for pedestrians and a slipping hazard for all road users, especially when wet.
hazards.location_in_image: Running longitudinally down the center of the roadway

hazards.name: Lack of Marked Crossings
hazards.description: There are no designated or marked locations for pedestrians to cross the street safely between residential blocks.

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions from Parked Cars
hazards.description: Parked vehicles along the curb line block sight lines between drivers and pedestrians attempting to cross.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the street along the curb

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental-style marked crosswalks at intersections to define pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk at corners to reduce crossing distance and move pedestrians into the driver's line of sight past parked cars.

interventions.title: ADA Compliant Curb Ramps
interventions.description: Install tactile warning strips and sloped ramps at all potential crossing points to ensure accessibility.

result.summary: The street is a residential corridor featuring brick row houses and a continuous sidewalk on the left. The roadway includes embedded streetcar tracks but lacks marked crosswalks, traffic signals, or any form of pedestrian crossing protection.

hazards.name: Streetcar tracks
hazards.description: Embedded tracks in the roadway can cause tripping for pedestrians or catch bicycle tires.

hazards.name: Lack of marked crossings
hazards.description: The absence of marked crosswalks leaves pedestrians without a designated or protected space to cross the street.

interventions.title: High-visibility crosswalks
interventions.description: Install painted crosswalks to clearly define pedestrian crossing areas and alert drivers.

interventions.title: Curb extensions
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk at intersections to reduce crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Street trees
interventions.description: Plant trees along the sidewalk to provide a physical and psychological buffer between pedestrians and the roadway.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment features wide sidewalks and mixed-use land use, but lacks robust crossing protection. Faded crosswalk markings and the presence of trolley tracks in the roadway create significant navigational hazards and reduced visibility for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Faded Crosswalk Markings
hazards.description: The painted crosswalk is significantly worn, reducing its visibility to approaching motorists.
hazards.location_in_image: Right foreground across the side street

hazards.name: Trolley Tracks
hazards.description: Metal tracks in the roadway can be slippery when wet and pose a trip hazard or a risk for bicycle tires.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the image running parallel to the main road

hazards.name: Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: Parked vehicles near the corner obstruct the view between pedestrians waiting to cross and oncoming traffic.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the curb line near the intersection

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk
interventions.description: Replace faded markings with continental or ladder-style high-visibility paint to improve driver awareness.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk at the corner to shorten the crossing distance and improve sightlines by moving pedestrians past parked cars.

interventions.title: Intersection Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces immediately adjacent to the crosswalk to ensure clear sightlines for all road users.

result.summary: The intersection features a marked zebra crosswalk and wide sidewalks adjacent to a modern multi-story building. While basic infrastructure like curb ramps is present, the lack of active traffic control and potential sightline obstructions from parked vehicles are notable.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Vehicles
hazards.description: Parked cars on the left side of the street are positioned close to the crosswalk, potentially obscuring pedestrians from oncoming drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the image, adjacent to the crosswalk.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces within 20 feet of the crosswalk to improve sightlines between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane to shorten the crossing distance and place pedestrians in a more visible position.
